rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that anyone away from the Kaaba must face its direction, side, or bearing.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن كل من غاب عنها أن يستقبل ناحيتها وشطرها وتلقاءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the direction is uncertain, a worshipper should infer it from available signs, including stars, winds, and mountains.
rows.anchor: فعليه أن يستدل على ذلك بكل ما يمكنه من النجوم والرياح والجبال

rows.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
rows.claim: A person praying in the Sacred Mosque should face and look at the Kaaba; looking at it is reported to be worship.
rows.anchor: فإنه يروى أن النظر إلى الكعبة عبادة قاله عطاء ومجاهد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some jurists held that an absent worshipper must face the Kaaba itself rather than only its direction.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا هل فرض الغائب استقبال العين أو الجهة فمنهم من قال بالأول

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects requiring the Kaaba itself as an impracticable obligation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهو ضعيف لأنه تكليف لما لا يصل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Facing the direction is correct because it is feasible, commanded by the verse, and confirmed by prayer rows much wider than the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال بالجهة وهو الصحيح لثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse commands people everywhere, east or west, to face the Kaaba's direction.
rows.anchor: أنه المأمور به في القرآن لقوله تعالى: { فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The long prayer row, certainly many times wider than the Kaaba, supports facing its direction rather than the exact structure.
rows.anchor: أن العلماء احتجوا بالصف الطويل الذي يعلم قطعا أنه أضعاف عرض البيت

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik and those agreeing with him use this verse to support looking straight ahead while praying, rather than at the place of prostration.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية حجة واضحة لما ذهب إليه مالك ومن وافقه في أن المصلي حكمه أن ينظر أمامه

rows.speaker: الثوري وأبو حنيفة والشافعي والحسن بن حي
rows.claim: Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi'i, and al-Hasan ibn Hayy recommend looking at the place of prostration.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري وأبو حنيفة والشافعي والحسن بن حي: يستحب أن يكون نظره

rows.speaker: شريك القاضي
rows.claim: Sharik al-Qadi assigns different gaze points by posture: prostration while standing, feet in bowing, nose in prostration, and lap when seated.
rows.anchor: وقال شريك القاضي: ينظر في القيام إلى موضع السجود، وفي الركوع إلى موضع قدميه

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says to look ahead: lowering the head diminishes required upright posture, while holding it up and straining the eyes downward is hardship; looking down is better for one able.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: إنما ينظر أمامه فإنه إن حنى رأسه ذهب بعض القيام المفترض عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given the Book here are Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب } يريد اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they know to be true is the change of the qibla from Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: يعني تحويل القبلة من بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that scripture taught them Muhammad was a prophet, so they knew he spoke and commanded only truth.
rows.anchor: أنهم لما علموا من كتابهم أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم نبي علموا أنه لا يقول إلا الحق ولا يأمر إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that they knew abrogation was permissible in their religion, even though some denied it, and thus knew the new qibla was valid.
rows.anchor: أنهم علموا من دينهم جواز النسخ وإن جحده بعضهم فصاروا عالمين بجواز القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not neglect people's deeds; the statement also carries a threat.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجهين فهو إعلام بأن الله تعالى لا يهمل أعمال العباد ولا يغفل عنها، وضمنه الوعيد.

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read with second-person ta, addressing either the People of the Book or Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «تعملون» بالتاء على مخاطبة أهل الكتاب أو أمة محمد

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use the third-person ya reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالياء من تحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A calamity is anything that hurts or befalls a believer; the source gives the related verbal forms.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { مصيبة } المصيبة: كل ما يؤذي المؤمن ويصيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musiba is the singular of masa'ib; masuba, with a damma on sad, is another form, and musab can mean affliction.
rows.anchor: والمصيبة واحدة المصائب. والمصوبة بضم الصاد مثل المصيبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs unanimously hamza the plural masa'ib although its root has waw, by analogy with an added letter; the original plural is masa'ib without hamza.
rows.anchor: وأجمعت العرب على همز المصائب، وأصله الواو كأنهم شبهوا الأصلي بالزائد

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited verse uses musab in a phrase about a man who brought greetings as an unjust tribute.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
أسليم إن مصابكم رجلا
أهدى السلام تحية ظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ṣāba, as in an arrow hitting paper, is a dialectal equivalent of aṣāba.
rows.anchor: وصاب السهم القرطاس يصيب صيبا لغة في أصابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A calamity is a misfortune that befalls a person, even if slight, and the word is used for evil.
rows.anchor: والمصيبة: النكبة ينكبها الإنسان وإن صغرت وتستعمل في الشر

words: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ikrima says the Prophet's lamp went out at night; he said the istirja, explaining that anything hurting a believer is a calamity.
rows.anchor: روى عكرمة: أن مصباح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انطفأ ذات ليلة فقال

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: Muslim's report says illness, fatigue, sickness, sorrow, and even anxiety afflicting a believer expiate sins; al-Qurtubi says this confirms the prior report's meaning.
rows.anchor: خرج مسلم عن أبي سعيد وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما أنهما سمعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

words: قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Majah transmits that whoever renews the istirja when recalling an old calamity receives the same reward as on the day it occurred.
rows.anchor: عن فاطمة بنت الحسين عن أبيها قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report through Fitr ibn Khalifa and Ata ibn Abi Rabah says that when calamity strikes, one should remember the Prophet's calamity, the greatest of calamities.
rows.anchor: إذا أصاب أحدكم مصيبة فليذكر مصابه بي فإنها من أعظم المصائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Umar affirms the Prophet's calamity is greater than every Muslim's later calamity: revelation ended, prophethood died, evil first appeared with Arab apostasy, and good began to diminish.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وصدق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن المصيبة به أعظم من كل مصيبة يصاب بها المسلم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id said that before they had finished brushing the dust from the Prophet's grave, their hearts already felt changed.
rows.anchor: ما نفضنا أيدينا من التراب من قبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of the poem cited from Abu al-Atahiya says calamities are universal and urges the sufferer to recall Muhammad and his calamity.
rows.anchor:
فإذا ذكرت محمدا ومصابه
فاذكر مصابك بالنبي محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made these words a refuge for those afflicted and a protection for those tried because they gather blessed meanings.
rows.anchor: جعل الله تعالى هذه الكلمات ملجأ لذوي المصائب، وعصمة للممتحنين لما جمعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first phrase affirms God's oneness, servitude to Him, and His ownership.
rows.anchor: فإن قوله: «إنا لله» توحيد وإقرار بالعبودية والملك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second phrase acknowledges human mortality, resurrection from graves, and certainty that all affairs return to God, as they belong to Him.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { وإنآ إليه راجعون } إقرار بالهلك على أنفسنا والبعث من قبورنا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says these words were not given to any prophet before Muhammad; had Jacob known them, he would not have lamented Joseph.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير رحمه الله تعالى: لم تعط هذه الكلمات نبيا قبل نبينا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Musa's report says that when a servant's child dies, God asks what the parent said; if he praised God and said the istirja, God orders a heavenly house called the House of Praise.
rows.anchor: حدثني الضحاك عن أبي موسى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports the Prophet taught a supplication asking God for reward through calamity and a better replacement, which God grants to a Muslim who says it.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم عن أم سلمة قالت سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Umm Salama report illustrates the glad tidings to the patient: God may provide a replacement, as He gave her the Prophet after Abu Salama died, or abundant reward, or both.
rows.anchor: فهذا تنبيه على قوله تعالى: وبشر الصابرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ṣalāt upon a servant means pardon, mercy, blessing, and honoring him in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: وصلاة الله على عبده: عفوه ورحمته وبركته وتشريفه إياه في الدنيا والآخرة.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God's ṣalāt means forgiveness and good praise.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الصلاة من الله عز وجل الغفران والثناء الحسن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praying over a dead person means praising him and supplicating for him.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الصلاة على الميت إنما هو الثناء عليه والدعاء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy is repeated with a different word to emphasize and fully convey the meaning.
rows.anchor: وكرر الرحمة لما اختلف اللفظ تأكيدا وإشباعا للمعنى كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary illustrates its point about repeated meaning with verses about concealing clear proofs and God hearing secret talk.
rows.anchor: من البينات والهدى [البقرة: 159]، وقوله: أم يحسبون أنا لا نسمع سرهم ونجواهم

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A cited poem uses ṣalāt for the Lord's prayer upon John and his followers.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: صلى على يحيى وأشياعه رب كريم وشفيع مطاع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes mercy here as lifting distress and meeting a person's need.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالرحمة كشف الكربة وقضاء الحاجة.

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: In Bukhari, Umar calls prayer and mercy the two equal portions, and guidance the additional topping.
rows.anchor: وفي البخاري وقال عمر رضي الله عنه: نعم العدلان ونعم العلاوة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar's two equal portions are prayer and mercy; the additional portion is guidance.
rows.anchor: أراد بالعدلين الصلاة والرحمة، وبالعلاوة الاهتداء.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation of guidance is attaining the right to reward and generous recompense.
rows.anchor: قيل: إلى استحقاق الثواب وإجزال الأجر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that guidance means calamities become easier and grief lighter.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى تسهيل المصائب وتخفيف الحزن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people ask about the One they worship, tell them He is near, rewards obedience, answers the supplicant, and knows a servant's fasting, prayer, and other deeds.
rows.anchor: المعنى وإذا سألوك عن المعبود فأخبرهم أنه قريب يثيب على الطاعة ويجيب الداعي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the verse followed Umar's intercourse with his wife after the night prayer, his regret and tears, and his report to the Prophet before the concession was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقال مقاتل: إن عمر رضي الله عنه واقع امرأته بعدما صلى العشاء فندم على ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account links the verse to people who ate after sleeping, contrary to the initial rule, then regretted it; the verse signaled repentance's acceptance and abrogation of that rule.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما وجب عليهم في الابتداء ترك الأكل بعد النوم فأكل بعضهم ثم ندم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Jews asked how their Lord could hear prayer if heaven was five hundred years away and each heaven equally thick; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال: قالت اليهود كيف يسمع ربنا دعاءنا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says people asked whether their Lord was near, so they could whisper, or far, so they must call loudly; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: سببها أن قوما قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أقريب ربنا

rows.speaker: عطاء وقتادة
rows.claim: Ata and Qatada say that after 40:60 was revealed, people asked at what time they should call upon God, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء وقتادة: لما نزلت:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God is near in answering prayer.
rows.anchor: فإني قريب } أي بالإجابة. وقيل بالعلم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God is near through His knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل بالعلم. وقيل: قريب من أوليائي بالإفضال والإنعام.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation is that God is near to His friends through favor and beneficence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قريب من أوليائي بالإفضال والإنعام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here supplication means worship and God's answering means acceptance of the worship.
rows.anchor: أي أقبل عبادة من عبدني فالدعاء بمعنى العبادة، والإجابة بمعنى القبول.

rows.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
rows.claim: Abu Dawud transmits from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir the Prophet's statement that supplication is worship, followed by the command to call on God.
rows.anchor: دليله ما رواه أبو داود عن النعمان بن بشير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in 40:60 about those too proud of worship refers to those too proud to supplicate.
rows.anchor: إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands and encourages supplication, names it worship, and promises to answer.
rows.anchor: فأمر تعالى بالدعاء وحض عليه وسماه عبادة، ووعد بأن يستجيب لهم.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ubada ibn al-Samit says this community, like the prophets, was promised an answer to prayer; it also contrasts their roles concerning hardship and witness.
rows.anchor: روى ليث عن شهر بن حوشب عن عبادة بن الصامت قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: خالد الربعي
rows.claim: Khalid al-Rab'i marvels that God commands supplication and promises an answer without stating a condition, unlike promises tied to faith and good works or sincere worship.
rows.anchor: وكان خالد الربعي يقول: عجبت لهذه الأمة في { ادعوني أستجب لكم } أمرهم بالدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities turned to their prophets to ask God for their needs.
rows.anchor: وكانت الأمم تقرع إلى أنبيائها في حوائجهم حتى تسأل الأنبياء لهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to answer does not require every supplicant to receive every specific thing requested.
rows.anchor: لا يقتضي الاستجابة مطلقا لكل داع على التفصيل، ولا بكل مطلوب على التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He does not love transgressors; al-Qurtubi counts anyone persisting in a major sin, knowingly or unknowingly, among them.
rows.anchor: وكل مصر على كبيرة عالما بها أو جاهلا فهو معتد، وقد أخبر أنه لا يحب المعتدين

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars understand the promise as God answering if He wills, as stated in 6:41, so the unrestricted wording is qualified elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: أجيب إن شئت كما قال: فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet supplicated for three things, received two, and was denied one; al-Qurtubi says details will follow in al-An'am.
rows.anchor: وقد دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ثلاث فأعطي اثنتين ومنع واحدة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the verse generally tells believers that their Lord answers supplications, hears them, knows their distress, and responds as He wills.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما مقصود هذا الإخبار تعريف جميع المؤمنين أن هذا وصف ربهم سبحانه أنه يجيب دعاء الداعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast is with calling on beings besides God who cannot respond.
rows.anchor: ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A master may answer a servant or a parent a child without granting the specific request, so answering and granting are distinct.
rows.anchor: وقد يجيب السيد عبده والوالد ولده ثم لا يعطيه سؤله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some form of answer necessarily occurs when prayer is made, since these are un-abrogated declarative statements and otherwise God would be a liar.
rows.anchor: لأن أجيب وأستجب خبر لا ينسخ فيصير المخبر كذابا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying that whoever is granted openness in supplication has the doors of response opened for him.
rows.anchor: من فتح له في الدعاء فتحت له أبواب الإجابة

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A revelation to David says God has bound Himself to answer anyone who calls, but if He answers wrongdoers, He curses them.
rows.anchor: وأوحى الله تعالى إلى داود: أن قل للظلمة من عبادي لا يدعوني فإني أوجبت على نفسي

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One view says every prayer is answered in one of three ways: granted now, stored for the afterlife, or offset by equivalent protection from harm.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إن الله يجيب كل الدعاء فإما أن تظهر الإجابة في الدنيا، وإما أن يكفر عنه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports that a Muslim who asks without sin or severing kin receives one of three outcomes; when asked if they should ask more, the Prophet replied that God is more generous.
rows.anchor: ما من مسلم يدعو بدعوة ليس فيها إثم ولا قطيعة رحم إلا أعطاه الله بها إحدى ثلاث

rows.speaker: أبو محمد عبد الحق
rows.claim: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq graded the Abu Sa'id report sound; Abu Umar says it appears in the Muwatta with a disconnected chain.
rows.anchor: وصححه أبو محمد عبد الحق، وهو في الموطأ منقطع السند.

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar presents the report as a connected exegesis of God's promise to answer in 40:60, with all three outcomes counting as response.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وهذا الحديث يخرج في التفسير المسند لقول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says every servant who prays is answered: worldly provision is granted if it is allotted to him, otherwise it is stored for him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كل عبد دعا أستجيب له فإن كان الذي يدعو به رزقا له في الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muslim's report from Abu Hurayra adds that prayer continues to be answered unless the supplicant asks for sin or severing kin, or becomes impatient and gives up.
rows.anchor: لا يزال يستجاب للعبد ما لم يدع بإثم أو قطيعة رحم ما لم يستعجل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Abu Dawud transmit from Abu Hurayra that a person remains answered unless he hastens, saying he prayed without receiving an answer.
rows.anchor: وروى البخاري ومسلم وأبو داود عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Scholars offer two readings of the answer promise: a necessary outcome among the three already mentioned, or the possibility of the specific request being granted.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا رحمة الله عليهم: يحتمل قوله «يستجاب لأحدكم» الإخبار عن وجوب وقوع الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, saying that no answer came denies all three outcomes and empties the supplication of each.
rows.anchor: بطل وقوع أحد هذه الثلاثة الأشياء وعري الدعاء من جميعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second reading, impatience prevents a specific answer because it shows despair, weak certainty, and discontent.
rows.anchor: ويمنع من ذلك قول الداعي: قد دعوت فلم يستجب لي لأن ذلك من باب القنوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlawful food and its like also prevent a supplication from being answered.
rows.anchor: قلت: ويمنع من إجابة الدعاء أيضا أكل الحرام وما كان في معناه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes a traveler who raises his hands and calls on God while eating, drinking, wearing, and being nourished with unlawful things, then asks how such a prayer could be answered.
rows.anchor: الرجل يطيل السفر أشعث أغبر يمد يديه إلى السماء يا رب يا رب ومطعمه حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith's question expresses how unlikely acceptance is for someone in that condition; answering requires conditions in the supplicant, prayer, and requested thing.
rows.anchor: وهذا استفهام على جهة الاستبعاد من قبول دعاء من هذه صفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplicant must know that only God can meet the need and that all intermediaries are under His control.
rows.anchor: أن يكون عالما بأن لا قادر على حاجته إلا الله، وأن الوسائط في قبضته ومسخرة بتسخيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplicant needs sincere intent and an attentive heart; God does not answer a heedless, distracted heart.
rows.anchor: وأن يدعو بنية صادقة وحضور قلب، فإن الله لا يستجيب دعاء من قلب غافل لاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other conditions on the supplicant are avoiding unlawful food and not tiring of supplication.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون مجتنبا لأكل الحرام، وألا يمل من الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested matter must be legally permissible to ask for and do; the cited report excludes sin and severing kinship, which includes Muslims' rights and wrongs.
rows.anchor: ومن شرط المدعو فيه أن يكون من الأمور الجائزة الطلب والفعل شرعا

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl al-Tustari lists seven conditions: humility, fear, hope, persistence, reverence, generality, and lawful food.
rows.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله التستري: شروط الدعاء سبعة: أولها التضرع والخوف والرجاء

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata likens supplication to a structure with pillars, wings, causes, and times: when these fit, it gains strength, ascends, and succeeds.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء: إن للدعاء أركانا وأجنحة وأسبابا وأوقاتا فإن وافق أركانه قوي

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata names the pillars as presence of heart, compassion, resignation, and humility; sincerity is its wings, pre-dawn its time, and blessings on Muhammad its cause.
rows.anchor: فأركانه حضور القلب والرأفة والاستكانة والخشوع، وأجنحته الصدق، ومواقيته الأسحار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account gives four conditions: guarding the heart in solitude, tongue among people, eyes from the forbidden, and stomach from unlawful food.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شرائطه أربع أولها حفظ القلب عند الوحدة، وحفظ اللسان مع الخلق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say supplication must be free of grammatical solecism, as a poem says a lion who calls his Lord with solecism gets no answer.
rows.anchor: أن يكون سليما من اللحن كما أنشد بعضهم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham explains unanswered prayers by listing disobedience, failure to follow the Prophet and Qur'an, ingratitude, neglect of the afterlife, complicity with Satan, lack of preparation for death, and preoccupation with others' faults.
rows.anchor: وقيل لإبراهيم بن أدهم: ما بالنا ندعو فلا يستجاب لنا؟ قال: لأنكم عرفتم الله فلم تطيعوه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali tells Nawf that God instructed David to require pure hearts, humble eyes, and clean hands from worshippers, and said He would not answer anyone while they wronged another creature.
rows.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه لنوف البكالي: يا نوف، إن الله أوحى إلى داود أن مر بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali warns Nawf against being a poet, tax official, police officer, collector, or customs collector; David's night prayer excluded those jobs and players of the tambourine or drum.
rows.anchor: يا نوف، لا تكونن شاعرا ولا عريفا ولا شرطيا ولا جابيا ولا عشارا

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Scholars say a supplicant should not qualify requests for forgiveness, mercy, or gifts with if You wish; he should ask decisively as someone in need.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: ولا يقل الداعي: اللهم أعطني إن شئت، اللهم اغفر لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding if You wish suggests indifference to God's mercy or gift, like asking someone whose help one does not need; the needy should be resolute.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإن في قوله: «إن شئت» نوع من الاستغناء عن مغفرته وعطائه ورحمته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction to make one's request resolutely and not say grant it if You wish, since no one can compel God.
rows.anchor: روى الأئمة واللفظ للبخاري عن أنس بن مالك قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muwatta also quotes the wording, O God forgive me if You wish and have mercy on me if You wish.
rows.anchor: اللهم اغفر لي إن شئت، اللهم ارحمني إن شئت

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Scholars say resolving to ask means striving in supplication and hoping for an answer, without despairing of God's mercy, since one asks the Generous.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: قوله «فليعزم المسألة» دليل على أنه ينبغي للمؤمن

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says knowledge of one's own faults should not deter prayer: God answered Iblis when he asked to be delayed until resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان ابن عيينة: لا يمنعن أحدا من الدعاء ما يعلمه من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likely times and circumstances for answered supplication include pre-dawn, breaking the fast, between call and commencement of prayer, Wednesday afternoon, distress, travel, illness, rain, and battle ranks.
rows.anchor: وللدعاء أوقات وأحوال يكون الغالب فيها الإجابة، وذلك كالسحر ووقت الفطر، وما بين الأذان والإقامة

rows.speaker: أم الدرداء
rows.claim: Umm al-Darda told Shahr ibn Hawshab to pray when he felt goosebumps, saying prayer is answered then.
rows.anchor: وروى شهر بن حوشب أن أم الدرداء قالت له: يا شهر، ألا تجد القشعريرة؟

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir says the Prophet prayed three times at the Conquest Mosque on Monday and Tuesday and was answered on Wednesday between prayers; Jabir sought that hour for grave troubles and recognized the answer.
rows.anchor: وقال جابر بن عبد الله: دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسجد الفتح ثلاثا يوم الإثنين ويوم الثلاثاء

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Abu Raja al-Khurasani interprets the command as let them pray to Me.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رجاء الخراساني: فليدعوا لي

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya interprets it as let them request that I answer; this is the usual seeking sense of the form استفعل, apart from exceptional forms such as istaghna Allah.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: المعنى فليطلبوا أن أجيبهم. وهذا هو باب «استفعل» أي طلب الشيء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Mujahid and others understand it as answering God's call to faith, obedience, and action.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره: المعنى فليجيبوا إلي فيما دعوتهم إليه من الإيمان أي الطاعة والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajaba and istajaba are synonymous; the cited line uses istajaba in the sense of answering.
rows.anchor: ويقال: أجاب واستجاب بمعنى ومنه قول الشاعر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sīn is extra and the lām is an imperative; it jussives the verb because it makes it future-only, like a conditional particle, or because it only precedes verbs.
rows.anchor: والسين زائدة واللام لام الأمر. وكذا «وليؤمنوا» وجزمت لام الأمر لأنها تجعل الفعل مستقبلا لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd is the opposite of error; the source gives two pronunciations and forms meaning guidance, direction, or the straightest road.
rows.anchor: والرشاد خلاف الغي. وقد رشد يرشد رشدا. ورشد بالكسر يرشد رشدا، لغة فيه.

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari records marashid as routes' destinations, arshad as the straighter road, rashda as legitimate birth, Umm Rashid as a mouse's nickname, and Banu Rashdan as an Arab clan.
rows.anchor: والمراشد: مقاصد الطرق. والطريق الأرشد: نحو الأقصد. وتقول: هو لرشدة.

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawi says rushd, rushd, and rashad mean guidance and uprightness, which explains the verse's hope that they will be guided.
rows.anchor: وقال الهروي: الرشد والرشد والرشاد: الهدى والاستقامة ومنه قوله: «لعلهم يرشدون».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaqifa has two verbal nouns, thaqfan and thuqfan; a thaqif laqif person is skilled at handling matters.
rows.anchor: يقال: ثقف يثقف ثقفا وثقفا، ورجل ثقف لقف: إذا كان محكما لما يتناوله من الأمور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is evidence that captured prisoners may be killed; al-Qurtubi defers the detailed discussion to al-Anfal.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على قتل الأسير، وسيأتي بيان هذا في «الأنفال» إن شاء الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The place from which they expelled the believers is Mecca.
rows.anchor: وأخرجوهم من حيث أخرجوكم } أي مكة.

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the addressees as the Emigrants and the pronoun as referring to Quraysh unbelievers.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: الخطاب للمهاجرين، والضمير لكفار قريش.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The persecution that drove believers toward disbelief and sought their apostasy is worse than killing.
rows.anchor: أي الفتنة التي حملوكم عليها وراموا رجوعكم بها إلى الكفر أشد من القتل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the believer's being led into persecution is worse than being killed; death is lighter than fitna for him.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: أي من أن يقتل المؤمن فالقتل أخف عليه من الفتنة

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another view says associating partners with God and disbelieving in Him is a greater sin than the killing for which believers were reproached.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: أي شركهم بالله وكفرهم به أعظم جرما وأشد من القتل الذي عيروكم به

rows.speaker: الطبري وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and others link the revelation to Amr ibn al-Hadrami's killing by Waqid ibn Abd Allah on the last day of Rajab during Abd Allah ibn Jahsh's expedition.
rows.anchor: في آخر يوم من رجب الشهر الحرام، حسب ما هو مذكور في سرية عبد الله بن جحش، على ما يأتي بيانه قاله الطبري وغيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists disagree over whether the prohibition on fighting at the Sacred Mosque was abrogated or remains operative.
rows.anchor: للعلماء في هذه الآية قولان: أحدهما: أنها منسوخة، والثاني: أنها محكمة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وطاوس
rows.claim: Mujahid and Tawus hold the verse operative: no one may be fought in the Sacred Mosque unless they fight first; al-Qurtubi says this follows the text and is correct.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: الآية محكمة، ولا يجوز قتال أحد في المسجد الحرام إلا بعد أن يقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions also hold that the verse remains operative.
rows.anchor: وهو الصحيح من القولين، وإليه ذهب أبو حنيفة وأصحابه.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a sound report from Ibn Abbas, the Prophet said Mecca was sanctified by God at creation, remains forbidden until the Resurrection, and fighting was permitted to him only for an hour on the day of its conquest.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم فتح مكة:

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the prohibition was abrogated by the command to kill the polytheists wherever they are found in 9:5.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الآية منسوخة بقوله تعالى: فإذا انسلخ الأشهر الحرم فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says this was first abrogated by the command to kill wherever found, then that command was abrogated by 9:5, allowing fighting to begin in the sanctuary; he notes Bara'a came two years after al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نسخها قوله تعالى: { واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم } ثم نسخ هذا قوله: { فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم }
